title: Schema fidelity & graceful tool-handoff playbook for streaming structured responses
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD-style acceptance playbook defining expected behaviors when the Redwood API emits streamed structured responses that invoke external tools/functions. Focus: schema fidelity, resumability, deterministic handoff semantics, error classification, and telemetry required for rollout to hosted and dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake: Every streaming response that emits structured frames MUST start with a single 'schema_manifest' frame that includes schema_id, schema_version, model_emitter_version, and an optional relaxed_fallback boolean. Consumers may reject streams where schema_id is unknown unless relaxed_fallback==true.

Frame envelope and ordering: All emitted frames MUST be self-describing and include these top-level fields: frame_type, seq_num (monotonic increasing integer), stream_id (UUID), timestamp_iso8601, and optional resume_token. Allowed frame_type values: schema_manifest, partial_object, commit_marker, tool_call, tool_result, error_frame, heartbeat.

Checkpointed commits: A commit_marker frame marks a consumer-visible stable checkpoint. Consumers MAY treat data prior to the most recent commit_marker as tentative. On resume, client supplies the last-acknowledged seq_num or resume_token; server MUST replay from the next seq_num and MUST not re-emit committed fragments as tentative.

Tool/function invocation envelope: tool_call frames MUST include call_id (UUID), idempotency_key (string), tool_name, declared_input_schema_id, declared_input_checksum, and invocation_mode (sync|async). call_id must be stable across retries for the same logical call. Tool gateways must return tool_result frames with matching call_id and status in {ok,recoverable_error,fatal_error}.

Idempotency and replay safety: If the client retransmits a resume_token that spans a previously-emitted tool_call, the platform MUST ensure either (a) the tool call is idempotent via idempotency_key or (b) the tool gateway provides a deduplication record and returns the original tool_result without performing duplicate side effects.

Schema mismatch handling: If the runtime detects a schema mismatch between declared_input_schema_id and the tool's observed input, or between emitted frames and the initial schema_manifest, it MUST emit an error_frame with classification 'schema_mismatch' and a suggested recovery action: {retry_with_schema: id | soft_fallback_to_unstructured}. If relaxed_fallback==true, emit a structured 'soft_fallback' frame containing best-effort payload and a clear signal that fidelity is degraded.

Partial/failed tool calls: For recoverable tool failures (e.g., transient network), the platform MUST attempt up to N retry_attempts configurable per-customer (default 2) with exponential backoff while preserving the same call_id and idempotency_key. Each retry attempt must emit a tool_call_retry frame that increments an attempt counter. If retries exhaust, emit tool_result with status 'recoverable_error' and include retry_count and last_error_code.

Fatal errors and graceful shutdown: For unrecoverable errors during streaming (e.g., model OOM, unhandled exception), emit an error_frame with classification 'fatal' and a human-readable message. Server must then close the stream with an explicit 'stream_closed' commit_marker that indicates terminal=true and final_error_code. Consumers must not attempt automatic resume for terminal=true streams.

Backpressure and flow control: Streaming endpoints MUST support a simple window header (X-Stream-Window) or equivalent frame indicating preferred outstanding frames. If server respects low window, it MUST flush partial frames as 'heartbeat' at least every 2s to maintain connection liveness. Large payload fragmentation rules must be respected (no single partial_object frame > 256KB unless chunked).

Observability contract: Each emitted stream must generate these telemetry events: stream_started, schema_manifest_received, tool_call_initiated (with tool_name, call_id), tool_call_completed, tool_call_failed, stream_resumed, stream_closed (with terminal flag). All events must include stream_id, customer_id, model_id, and route_id for debugging and SLIs.

E2E tests and contracts: Contract tests (automated) must exercise: schema handshake acceptance, resume from mid-stream including in-flight tool calls, dedup behavior for idempotent vs non-idempotent tools, schema_mismatch soft fallback path, fatal-error terminal behavior, and windowed backpressure. Golden fixtures must exist in integration-tests/structured-output/fixtures.

Cross-environment parity: The same acceptance criteria MUST hold for hosted API and Redwood Dedicated; where Dedicated customers have custom tool gateways, integration steps must be documented in dedicated-onboarding checklists.

Backward compatibility: New schema versions must support a 'compatibility_policy' value in manifest: {strict,semver_compatible,permissive}. If strict, server must reject client resume attempts across incompatible versions and emit a schema_mismatch error_frame.

Security: Tool invocation arguments MUST be redacted in telemetry unless flagged allow_telemetry=true by customer. KMS/HSM keys and secrets must never be serialized in frames. Security review required before GA for any change to tool-call envelope fields.
test_scenarios: Resume mid-stream where last acked seq_num is the seq_num of a tool_call which completed before the disconnect: ensure re-resume does not re-run side effects and returns original tool_result.
Consumer disconnects after partial_object frames but before commit_marker; on resume consumer receives the same tentative frames followed by commit_marker once model completes.
Tool gateway returns 502 intermittently: platform retries twice with exponential backoff and includes tool_call_retry frames; final result is recoverable_error with retry_count=2 in tool_result.

Injected schema_manifest with compatibility_policy=strict and downgraded model_emitter_version; server rejects resume and emits schema_mismatch error_frame with suggested action 'fetch_compatible_model'.
High-throughput test: 5k concurrent streaming connections with small frames; verify telemetry scales and heartbeat intervals are preserved under load.
Security leak test: verify that telemetry sanitization removes any key-like patterns and that allow_telemetry gate prevents emission of raw tool args.
Golden contract test: consumer harness validates that commit_marker seq_num increments are stable across 1000 replay iterations.
Dedicated onboarding test: run an integration harness against a customer-provided tool gateway that records deduplication behavior and verify idempotency contract.
telemetry_and_slo: SLO: 99.9% of streams resume successfully within 2s of reconnect when last frame was a commit_marker.
SLO: schema_mismatch_rate <= 0.05% per 1M streamed frames in GA region.

Metrics to emit: metric.streams_started, metric.streams_resumed, metric.tool_calls_initiated, metric.tool_calls_succeeded, metric.tool_calls_retried, metric.schema_mismatch_count, metric.streams_terminated_fatal.
Tracing: every tool_call must include a trace_id that links model emission, tool gateway RPC, and final tool_result frame for distributed traces.
Alerting: high schema_mismatch_rate ( > 0.5% over 10m) triggers P1 pager and automatic rollbacks to previous schema_manifest emitter if rollback allowed by compatibility_policy.
rollback_and_upgrade_notes: When changing schema_manifest default policies, rollout must be staged: 10% of traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated fallback to previous manifest on >0.2% uplift in schema_mismatch_rate.
Upgrades to frame envelope fields are additive only. Removing fields requires a deprecation cycle: 2 weeks for staging, 2 weeks for GA and opt-in, with deprecation notices in client SDKs.
Database migration: resume_token encoding changes must be backward readable for 90 days to support long-lived client sessions.
